briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical development of the past 24 hours is a significant Houthi missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, resulting in reported casualties, extensive damage to Terminal 3, and the complete closure of the airport. This attack has led to widespread flight cancellations, international travel warnings, and a declared "broad operation" by the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, sharply escalating regional tensions. Concurrently, the US has pressured Israel for a unilateral strike on Iran, further contributing to a highly volatile environment.

IRAN
Iran's Army Ground Forces Commander, Brigadier General Ali Jahanshahi, reported the deployment of over 50 combat and support units along the country's borders from northwest to southwest, eastern regions, and the Makran coast, stating a high level of readiness. President Masoud Pezeshkian emphasized the need for Iran to stand firm against bullying and strengthen its scientific and technological capabilities, urging regional diplomacy beyond meetings to manage crises and prevent escalation. Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi called Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu a "wanted war criminal" with Arab, American, and Iranian blood on his hands, accusing him of desperately seeking to save himself with US resources. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned the US against underestimating Iran's ancient civilization. A new mural in Tehran's Enghelab Square commemorates "Operation Al-Aqsa Flood" (Oct 7 anniversary) and depicts Israel's international isolation, specifically targeting PM Netanyahu at the UN. An Iraqi resistance group praised Iran's control and management of the Strait of Hormuz. US officials, according to Bloomberg, assess Iran has maintained its ability to produce and develop new missiles and drones, and to replenish its arsenal, a claim the White House denied. Trump stated Iran "either gives us everything or they don't exist any longer" and claimed the US has "complete control" of the Strait of Hormuz, preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons. Russia's Security Council Deputy Chairman Dmitry Medvedev noted "unprecedented" Iran-Russia relations and 90% SCO trade in national currencies, advocating shared financial/legal mechanisms against Western sanctions. Separately, 19 Iranian oil tankers are reportedly experiencing shortages of water, food, and fuel near Sri Lanka.

ISRAEL
President Isaac Herzog announced he will award FlyDubai pilot Captain Smith Machhar the "Presidential Medal for Civilian Bravery" for his actions on FlyDubai Flight FZ1073. The UAE has confirmed the Omani co-pilot of this flight planned a suicide operation to crash the aircraft into Tel Aviv's Ben Gurion Airport, inspired by 9/11. The IDF and Shin Bet confirmed the elimination of Mohammad Abu Shallouf, an Islamic Jihad company commander who participated in the October 7 "massacre," and Musa Atef Musa Abu Dan, a Hamas Nukhba operative, in Khan Yunis, Gaza. An IDF interceptor was launched at a suspicious aerial target in southern Lebanon where IDF forces are operating; results are under review. In the Syria-Lebanon border area, the IDF air-attacked Syrian operative Yusuf Ali al-Hassoun, who was promoting terror plots against Israeli citizens and IDF forces in southern Syria under Iranian direction. The IDF also eliminated a militant who crossed the "Yellow Line" in northern Gaza. MK Gadi Eisenkot has demanded the Attorney General conclude an investigation into Tzahi Braverman's alleged protocol forgery before the upcoming elections, claiming a "systematic pattern" with the PM's knowledge. Benny Gantz stated he would "run until the end" in the elections. Maariv reported that the US pressured Israel to launch a unilateral strike on Iran in the past two weeks to avert US political fallout before November midterm elections, potentially delaying Israel's own October 27 elections; this demand was reportedly dropped due to warnings from IDF Chief Eyal Zamir.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces eliminated two militants in Khan Yunis, Mohammad Abu Shallouf (Islamic Jihad commander, 7 October participant) and Musa Atef Musa Abu Dan (Hamas Nukhba). Five fatalities and several injuries were reported in an Israeli strike in western Gaza City. Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas issued a presidential decree canceling the Palestinian legislative elections scheduled for November 28, 2026, and postponing them to September 11, 2027, to align with presidential elections. Fatah spokesperson Jamal Nazzal attributed the postponement to "Israel thwarting the preparation of necessary conditions." Over 100 international organizations stated the Gaza ceasefire "exists only on paper" due to ongoing Israeli attacks and aid restrictions. A US "charity" reportedly plans to use AI to monitor Gaza classrooms for anti-Israeli language, raising privacy and academic freedom concerns.

LEBANON
An Israeli military drone strike near the Lebanon-Syria border injured six people, including five Syrian nationals and one Lebanese citizen. IDF forces operating in southern Lebanon launched an interceptor at a suspicious aerial target; results are pending. Lebanese security forces seized hundreds of kilograms of C-4 and TNT explosives from a vehicle in Dahr al-Baidar, Bekaa Valley, arresting two Hezbollah suspects.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The IDF air-attacked Syrian operative Yusuf Ali al-Hassoun, who was promoting terror plots against Israeli citizens and IDF forces in southern Syria under Iranian direction. Iraqi Prime Minister Al-Zaidi is scheduled to visit Saudi Arabia and Kuwait this weekend. A large dust storm entered Iraq from Syria. Iraqi helicopter flights were observed over Karbala following the PM's arrival. Iraqi Hashd al-Shaabi forces and Federal Police engaged ISIS elements in Hawija, Kirkuk province, with reported ISIS casualties. A US official stated that withdrawing from Iraq protects US forces from militias if tensions with Iran escalate.

GULF STATES
King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, was struck by a Houthi missile attack, causing an "enormous explosion" and extensive damage to Terminal 3. Reports indicate 10 deaths and 45 injured, with 5 in intensive care, leading to the complete evacuation of the airport and cancellation of 221 flights, including those from Turkish and Kuwaiti airlines. The Saudi Civil Aviation Authority temporarily suspended all operations. The US, British, German, Canadian, and Spanish embassies issued warnings to their citizens to avoid the airport. Satellite imagery confirmed smoke rising from the Ayn Dar oil field west of Buqayq City, and columns of smoke from Saudi Arabia’s Ghawar oil field (world's largest conventional oil field) after reported Houthi strikes on the Shedgum gas plant. These attacks reportedly disabled the strategic East-West oil pipeline and halted loading operations at Yanbu port. The Houthis claimed all Saudi airports are now non-operational and issued a "humanitarian flights only" decree for Riyadh, permitting an air ambulance to land. Saudi air force reportedly conducted four missile strikes in Haraf Sufyan (Amran province), Bab al-Mandab, and villages in Razih district (Saada province) in Yemen. The Saudi-led coalition announced a "broad operation" against Houthi elements to "dismantle and destroy the ballistic missile network." The Wall Street Journal reported that Houthis "relentlessly attack Saudi airports," aiming to cut off air links, raising concerns for Saudi Arabia's upcoming Future Investment Initiative conference. A Saudi political source told Al-Modon that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman requested Syrian fighters from Syrian President Ahmed al-Shara during his visit to assist in the fight against Houthis. Flight disruptions were reported at Jeddah, Riyadh, Al-Ahsa, and Dammam airports.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Houthi Missile Strike on Riyadh Airport:** King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was directly hit by a Houthi missile, causing reported deaths (up to 10), injuries (up to 45), damage to Terminal 3, and complete operational suspension, leading to international travel warnings.
2.  **Ghawar Oil Field Attack:** Satellite imagery and reports confirm strikes on Saudi Arabia's Ghawar oil field and Shedgum gas plant, causing fires and reportedly disabling the strategic East-West oil pipeline.
3.  **US Pressure on Israel for Unilateral Iran Strike:** Maariv reported US pressure on Israel for a unilateral military strike on Iran, aiming to avoid US political fallout before November midterms, though the demand was reportedly dropped.
4.  **US-Russia Diesel Deal:** President Trump announced an agreement with Russian President Putin for Russia to supply millions of tons of diesel fuel to global and US markets, with General License No. 135 issued by OFAC to lift sanctions on Russian diesel imports until April 7, 2027.
5.  **Palestinian Elections Postponed:** PA President Mahmoud Abbas cancelled legislative elections scheduled for November 28, 2026, postponing them to September 11, 2027.
6.  **IDF Eliminations in Gaza and Syria:** The IDF eliminated Mohammad Abu Shallouf (Islamic Jihad company commander) and Musa Atef Musa Abu Dan (Hamas Nukhba) in Khan Yunis, Gaza, and Syrian operative Yusuf Ali al-Hassoun in the Syria-Lebanon border region.
7.  **Iranian Military Readiness:** Iran's Army Ground Forces Commander announced the deployment of over 50 combat and support units along the country's borders, emphasizing high readiness.
8.  **FlyDubai Hijack Plot Revelation:** The UAE confirmed the FlyDubai co-pilot intended a 9/11-inspired suicide attack on Ben Gurion Airport, prompting Israel to review airline crew backgrounds.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The immediate threat of regional escalation remains extremely high. The Houthi missile attack on Riyadh's international airport and the Ghawar oil field demonstrates a significant escalation of the Yemen conflict with direct economic and civilian impact on Saudi Arabia. This directly increases the likelihood of a robust Saudi and coalition response, possibly involving Pakistan and Turkey, against Houthi strongholds, including Sana'a. The US pressure on Israel for a unilateral strike on Iran, despite being reportedly dropped, indicates a persistent inclination towards military action against Iranian capabilities. Iran's reported maintenance of missile and drone production, coupled with its "unprecedented" strategic partnership with Russia, sets red lines for potential adversaries. US warnings to citizens to leave Iran immediately and increased military alert levels reported by Iranian state media and civilian sources suggest a perceived imminent threat of conflict. The alleged Houthi mine-laying in Bab al-Mandab, a critical choke point, and Iran's claims of Strait of Hormuz control amplify maritime risks. The deep internal political divisions in both Israel (approaching elections) and Iran (economic crisis, internal dissent) add unpredictable variables to decision-making in a crisis.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States:** President Trump announced a deal with Russian President Putin for significant Russian diesel exports to the US and global markets, lifting related sanctions. This move was criticized by Ukrainian President Zelensky as "weak" and a "happy birthday present for Putin," leading to a Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian oil refinery in Rostov. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner reportedly threatened Ukraine with cessation of intelligence sharing if attacks on Russian oil facilities continued. The US Treasury's OFAC issued General License No. 135 authorizing Russian diesel imports until April 7, 2027. Trump fiercely criticized the Nobel Peace Prize committee for not awarding him, claiming he ended eight wars and deserves multiple awards, while disparaging Nobel laureate Navi Pillay as an Israel-hater. The US imposed new sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), a move rejected by the ICC and condemned globally. The US State Department issued an alert urging American citizens to "under no circumstances travel to Iran" and to "immediately depart."
**Gulf States:** Saudi Arabia's airports, particularly King Khalid International in Riyadh, were subject to Houthi attacks, causing closures and international travel warnings. Saudi-led coalition declared "broad operations" against Houthi missile networks. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman reportedly sought Syrian fighters from Syria's President Ahmed al-Shara to aid against Houthis.
**Europe:** Germany, Canada, and Spain advised their citizens to avoid Riyadh airport. The Netherlands and EU Council President Antonio Costa stated intent to protect the ICC against US sanctions. Finland's PM Petri Orpo called for stopping tourism visas for Russian citizens. The EU faces potential winter gas shortfalls.
**Russia:** President Putin reportedly conveyed Iran's stance on a potential resolution to the conflict to President Trump, coordinated with President Pezeshkian. Dmitry Medvedev highlighted "unprecedented" Iran-Russia relations and a global shift to multipolarity away from Western dominance.
**International Organizations:** The ICC rejected US sanctions, denouncing them as obstructing justice. Over 100 humanitarian and human rights organizations criticized the Gaza ceasefire as "existing only on paper."

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
**Contradictions and Unverified Claims:**
*   **Iran's Missile/Drone Capabilities:** Bloomberg reported that Iran maintained its missile and drone production capabilities despite US/Israeli attacks, a claim explicitly "rejected" by the White House which stated Iran's "production infrastructure has been destroyed." This represents a direct contradiction from official sources.
*   **Riyadh Airport Casualties:** Initial reports of the Riyadh airport attack varied significantly: "dozens injured," "at least 5 in intensive care," "around 10 fatalities," "45 wounded." While some confirmed deaths, precise numbers remain fluid.
*   **Tehran Explosions/GPS Disruption:** Multiple unverified reports of "explosions," "anti-aircraft fire," "smoke," and "severe GPS disruption" in Eastern Tehran and other cities (Yazd) circulated on social media channels affiliated with Iranian opposition. These claims lack official confirmation and could be misinterpreted sounds or deliberate disinformation.
*   **Imminent War Predictions:** Several sources, including an IRIB reporter and an "analyst for the UAE," made unverified predictions about an imminent attack on Iran "tonight" or "tomorrow." These should be treated with extreme caution as they are often speculative or propaganda.
*   **Evacuation of Tehran Police Stations:** Unverified reports claimed several police stations in districts 7 and 8 of Tehran were evacuated, either as a precaution or due to an unknown threat.
*   **Hormuz Control:** While Trump claimed "complete control" of the Strait of Hormuz, an Iraqi resistance group simultaneously claimed Iran was "tightening the noose" around US/allies with its control of the Strait, indicating conflicting narratives over effective control.

**Propaganda Indicators:**
*   **Trump's Nobel Rants:** Trump's repeated, lengthy, and self-aggrandizing rants about not receiving the Nobel Peace Prize, accusing the committee of bias and discrediting the laureate, serve as clear propaganda reinforcing his image.
*   **Iran's Al-Aqsa Flood Mural:** The new mural in Tehran linking the October 7 attack to "Al-Aqsa Flood" and depicting Netanyahu's isolation is a clear propaganda piece aimed at boosting morale and reinforcing anti-Israeli sentiment.
*   **Houthi Claims of Saudi Airport Control:** The Houthi spokesperson Yahya Sarie's statement that "only flights authorized by Sana'a" can land in Riyadh airport, and that "all Saudi airports are out of order," are exaggerated claims intended to demoralize the enemy and rally supporters.

**Reporting Gaps:**
*   Details on the specific types of Houthi missiles used in the Riyadh attack are not provided.
*   The extent of damage to Saudi aircraft or airport infrastructure beyond Terminal 3 is not fully detailed in all reports, though some noted "several planes damaged."
*   Specifics on the "broad operation" launched by the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen are lacking, beyond general targeting of Houthi capabilities.
*   The exact nature and outcome of the IDF interceptor in southern Lebanon are "under review," indicating a reporting gap.
*   The connection, if any, between the Russian diesel deal and a potential US-Iran conflict resolution mentioned by Putin and Pezeshkian remains unclear.
